tools.name: search_leads
tools.description: Run a live search for local businesses by niche + city (e.g. query 'electrician', location 'Austin, TX'). Returns the first batch immediately with a search_id; more results are found and verified in the background — every email is SMTP-checked and every phone verified with line type + carrier. Spend

tools.name: get_search_results
tools.description: Fetch a search's leads with verification filled in as enrichment progresses. Poll until enrichment is 'complete'. Each lead includes verified emails (SMTP status), verified phones (line type + carrier), owner name where identified, socials, and the business profile.

tools.name: enrich_domains
tools.description: Already have businesses? Pass up to 10 website domains to run the full enrichment + verification pipeline on them (verified emails + phones, owner name, socials). Costs 1 lead per domain. Returns a search_id to poll with get_search_results.

tools.name: query_leads
tools.description: Search ALL leads the account has ever collected (across every search) with filters and sorting — no new search is run and no leads are spent. Filter fields include: name, category, city, state, rating, reviews, website, claimed, owner_name, phone_1, email_1, email_status, phone_1_type, google_cid. O

tools.name: export_leads
tools.description: Push leads into a connected destination: 'close' (CRM — uses the account's saved field mapping), 'ghl' (GoHighLevel sub-account), 'google_sheets' (new spreadsheet, or pass spreadsheet_id for one LeadMarina created before), or a file — 'csv' | 'xlsx' | 'json' (emailed to the account owner + download

tools.name: list_searches
tools.description: The account's recent searches (id, niche, location, result count, when) — use a search_id with get_search_results or export_leads.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: What the account has left, and when it resets. On a plan with a rate limit (no monthly quota) this is the leads left in the current 7-day period; on a metered plan it is the monthly allotment remaining.

tools.name: list_views
tools.description: The account's saved views from the leads table — each a named set of filters the user already built (e.g. 'Roofers with a mobile number'). Returns each view's filter conditions in the exact shape query_leads and export_leads accept, so "export my Hot Leads view to Close" works without rebuilding the

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: Which export destinations this account has connected (Close, GoHighLevel, Google Sheets) and whether each is ready to receive leads. Check this BEFORE export_leads or create_automation with a CRM destination — those fail if the integration isn't connected, and Close additionally needs one manual exp

tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: The account's automations — saved searches that re-run on a schedule and export themselves. Shows each one's niche, cities, cadence, destination, whether it's active, when it next runs, and how the last run went.

tools.name: create_automation
tools.description: Create an automation: re-run a search on a schedule and send the results somewhere automatically. Pass cities as plain strings (e.g. ['Austin, TX', 'Dallas, TX']) — they're resolved for you. IT SPENDS LEADS ON EVERY RUN, one per result, so confirm the niche, cities and cadence with the user before c

tools.name: update_automation
tools.description: Pause an automation (active=false) so it stops running and stops spending leads, or resume it (active=true). Pausing is the safe way to stop an automation you might want back — use delete_automation only when the user wants it gone for good.

tools.name: delete_automation
tools.description: Permanently delete an automation. This cannot be undone — confirm with the user first, and prefer update_automation with active=false if they only want it to stop for now. Leads already collected by past runs are kept; only the schedule is removed.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_leads, get_search_results, query_leads, create_automation · Private data: export_leads, list_integrations, create_automation · Public sink: search_leads, query_leads, create_automation · Destructive: search_leads, enrich_domains, query_leads, list_automations, create_automation, delete_automation.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_leads, get_search_results, query_leads, create_automation · Private data: export_leads, list_integrations, create_automation · Public sink: search_leads, query_leads, create_automation · Destructive: search_leads, enrich_domains, query_leads, list_automations, create_automation, delete_automation

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
